textPlacement.assessment: Both ages preserve two fitting pieces, welcome help and an easier alternative without inventing a separate jigsaw starting age or requiring adult puzzle strategies.

The summary keeps supervision and touch-based interest central, while the differing two and two-and-a-half descriptions remain visible without becoming a test.
Spoken-language readiness remains explicit, and the invitation treats remembering as an unhurried shared conversation rather than a recall or naming test.
Both contexts retain seated supervision, handles, adult-held card and opening-and-closing as sufficient exploration while keeping the source age differences visible.

Placing bolts remains a sufficient beginning, with supervised turning and grading available without requiring every match or movement.
The activity preserves supervised stretching and child-chosen arrangements, with later patterns and owning the equipment left optional.
